findings.reason: §6 must say whether the dimension reads `clone_matches` as its measured input, or why the LLM-judged dimension and the deterministic detector are deliberately independent; the plan cites neither and so hides that two reuse instruments now exist.
findings.text: §6 defines a `reuse` code-review dimension that scores at most 0..20 and at most 5 when "an added definition re-implements a capability the repository already owns", yet the plan's own §4 already landed `reckon/clones.py`, a deterministic six-line normalised clone detector whose stated purpose is "a private copy is a review signal", and promotion already records its result as `clone_matches`; §6 names neither

findings.reason: §3 should state that a function-local delegate counts as reuse and record the import-cycle reason, or direct the callers to `metering.run_streams` directly; as written the section proposes a replacement it does not deliver.
findings.text: §3 says `metering.run_streams` replaces the promotion and ledger copies, but the landed design keeps two thin function-local wrappers — `reckon/crew/promotion.py:3421 _run_streams(path)` and `reckon/ledger.py:3161 _run_streams(run_id, streams_root)` — each adapting a different call shape and importing `metering` inside the function to dodge the facade import cycle; §3's text names no such wrapper and its done-when ("one implementation per concept, with any retained exception listed with its reason") is ambiguous about whether a delegate counts, which is the open question comment `c-awrbiw-parsers-and-writer-landed` leaves unresolved

thin_wrapper-1.reason: section 3 is still open on this plan and its two function-local run_streams delegates belong to that section's remaining node, which will either state the facade import-cycle reason for a delegate or route the callers to metering.run_streams directly; section 6 does not touch them

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §2 and §3 hide each shared policy behind one small interface (`reckon/_timestamps.py:parse_utc`, `reckon/_store.py:write_json_atomically`, `reckon/crew/metering.py:run_streams`, `reckon/_observations.py:optional_number`), and §6 adds one entry to the existing `REVIEW_DIMENSIONS` registry rather than a new subsystem.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan names the owner of each capability it touches (`reckon/_timestamps.py`, `reckon/_store.py`, `reckon/crew/metering.py`, `reckon/_observations.py`, `reckon/crew/review.py`) and extends each rather than forking; §3 defers its census re-run to §2 ("as in §2") so one pin serves both thresholds.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — supplied counts public_definitions 1473, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §6 adds a review dimension and a `gates.dimension_floors` key, none of which is in a counted family (`interface_counts.interfaces` counts command/group decorators, option decorators, `format_refusal` codes and MCP view names), and it names the clause it merges — the `fit` reuse clause from `the-orchestrator-orchestrates` §4 moves into the new dimension.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2/§3 cite the structural census and the owners they extend (`reckon/_store.py`, `reckon/crew/metering.py`, `reckon/_observations.py`), and §6 cites the landed `fit` reuse clause, but §6 adds an LLM-scored `reuse` dimension without citing `reckon/clones.py`, the deterministic clone detector §4 of this same plan already landed.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3 states `metering.run_streams` replaces the promotion and the ledger copies, but the design that landed keeps two thin function-local delegating wrappers over it, whose signature adaptation and import-cycle justification §3's own text does not carry.
